/-!
# Erdős Problem 562

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/562](https://www.erdosproblems.com/562)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Combinatorics Filter Real
open scoped Asymptotics

namespace Erdos562

/--
Let $R_r(n)$ denote the $r$-uniform hypergraph Ramsey number: the minimal $m$ such that if we
$2$-colour all edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $m$ vertices then there must be some
monochromatic copy of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Prove that, for $r \ge 3$,
$$ \log_{r-1} R_r(n) \asymp_r n, $$
where $\log_{r-1}$ denotes the $(r-1)$-fold iterated logarithm.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_562 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ r ≥ 3, (fun n ↦ log^[r - 1] (hypergraphRamsey r n)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos562

reformulations.difference: The imported hypergraphRamsey definition quantifies over colorings of all finite subsets of Fin m, whereas the source colors only the r-element edges.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Only subsets of cardinality r enter the monochromaticity condition. Restricting an arbitrary coloring to those subsets, and conversely extending an edge-coloring by false elsewhere, proves equivalence of the coloring predicates. Consequently the sets of admissible m, and their infima, coincide. Both the predicate equivalence and equality of the resulting Ramsey numbers were proved in the scratch file.

review.notes: The sole theorem matches the cited source's exact LaTeX, including r ≥ 3, r−1 iterated logarithms, and constants allowed to depend on r. Finite Ramsey's theorem ensures the defining infimum is over a nonempty set. Since R_r(n) ≥ n, each fixed iterated logarithm is eventually positive; totalized logarithms and norm-based Θ therefore preserve the claim. Boundary proofs, finite-coloring computations, and the positive two-sided-bounds interpretation of Θ were checked in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, which compiles successfully.
